claim.pdf_says: *> implicit filler ...1               1 1 1 1 1  1     02 PIC 1(5)   (five bit marks charted under bit positions 4-8, then the byte number 1)
claim.markdown_says: *> implicit filler ...1           1 1 1 1  1     02 PIC 1(5)   (only four bit marks)
claim.why_it_matters: One bit mark was lost from the first implicit-filler row of the first bit-alignment figure, so the chart now shows four filler bit positions while its own annotation says '02 PIC 1(5)'. The equivalent row in the second figure on the same page ('*> implicit filler ...           1 1 1 1 1  1     02 PIC 1(5)') still carries all five, confirming the drop. The figure exists precisely to show how many bits the implicit filler occupies, so a miscount defeats its purpose.

verdict.reasoning: Attempted refutation on every available ground and the claim survived all of them. (1) Not a reflow/adjacent-line artifact: I ran a pixel-column ink profile over the printed row at 300 dpi and against the figure's own 'Bit position 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8' header. The header digits sit at x = 1286, 1329, 1373, 1417, 1461, 1505, 1548, 1591 (pitch ~43.5 px). The first figure's first implicit-filler row has exactly FIVE glyph runs in the bit grid, at x = 1410, 1453, 1497, 1541, 1585 (widths 13-14 px, i.e. single digits, pitch 43-44 px), i.e. bit positions 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, followed by a separate run at x = 1651 which is the 'Byte # in data item' column value 1. The corresponding row of the second figure profiles identically: five marks at x = 1417, 1461, 1505, 1549, 1591 plus the byte column at 1651. So the PDF prints five marks in BOTH rows. (2) Not a misquote: the markdown line is verbatim as claimed. Canonical specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 44234 is '     *> implicit filler ...1           1 1 1 1  1     02 PIC 1(5)' with standalone '1' tokens at string indices 27, 39, 41, 43, 45, 48 - index 27 is the stray '1' fused to the ellipsis (which the PDF also prints, at x = 1008, far left of bit column 1 at x = 1286, so it is NOT a displaced fifth mark), indices 39/41/43/45 are FOUR grid marks, and index 48 is the byte number. The parallel line 44255 has marks at 38, 40, 42, 44, 46 (FIVE) plus the byte number at 49. Five marks in the PDF versus four in the markdown: one glyph genuinely lost. (3) Not a formatting/alignment quibble: the markdown never preserves absolute column alignment anywhere in these figures (line 44255's five marks land under header bits 2-6, and the item-2 row's mark lands under bit 2 rather than bit 3), so alignment is not the load-bearing property - the COUNT is, because the count is what the '02 PIC 1(n)' annotation asserts. (4) Every other filler row on the page has a mark count that matches its own annotation - 7 marks for PIC 1(7), 3 for PIC 1(3), 5 for PIC 1(5) in figure 2, 2 for PIC 1(2), 6 for PIC 1(6), 7 for PIC 1(7) - which makes this row the sole outlier and rules out a systematic transcription convention. (5) Meaning does change locally: the figure's whole purpose is to chart how many bits the implicit filler occupies, and item-1 pic 11 (bits 1-2) + item-2 pic 1 (bit 3) leaves bits 4-8 = 5 filler bits, so the four-mark row is internally self-contradictory. Severity 'cosmetic' is nevertheless correct: this is a non-normative worked example, the row's own '02 PIC 1(5)' annotation, the intact byte-number column, the identical row in the second figure, and the later 'implicit filler USAGE BIT PIC 1(5)' listing all still carry the correct value, so no normative rule is misstated and no compiler behavior is derivable incorrectly from the surviving text.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed as described, with two clarifications. The PDF's first implicit-filler row of the first bit-alignment figure prints five bit marks under bit positions 4-8 followed by the byte-number 1; the markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 44234) prints only four, while retaining the '02 PIC 1(5)' annotation. Clarification 1: the stray '1' fused to the ellipsis ('...1') is present in the PDF too - it is an ISO typesetting oddity at x=1008, well left of bit column 1 at x=1286, faithfully carried into the transcription - so it is not the displaced fifth mark and does not restore the count. Clarification 2: the transcription does not preserve absolute column alignment in any of these figures, so the defect is strictly the lost glyph (four marks where the PDF has five), not a shifted column. Fix: restore the fifth mark on line 44234 so the row reads '*> implicit filler ...1           1 1 1 1 1  1     02 PIC 1(5)'.
